title: C# Questions & Answers - Polymorphism
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on polymorphism in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: The capability of an object in Csharp to take number of different forms and hence display behaviour as according is known as ___________

options.text: Encapsulation
Polymorphism
Abstraction
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Polymorphism is the ability of a reference to work with objects of different types (overloading at compile time, overriding at run time).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
sample.x is 100, sample.y is 150, and newspaper.x hides sample.x so the unqualified x in Main is 1000.

Output:

100  150  1000

questions.question: Which of the following keyword is used to change data and behavior of a base class by replacing a member of the base class with a new derived member?

options.text: Overloads
Overrides
new
base

questions.explanation: The new modifier hides an inherited member. override replaces a virtual/abstract member for polymorphic dispatch. overloads is not a C# keyword.

questions.question: Correct way to overload +operator?

options.text: public sample operator + (sample a, sample b)
public abstract operator + (sample a,sample b)
public static sample operator + (sample a, sample b)
all of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Only the static operator+ form is valid. Operator methods must be public and static.

questions.question: What will be the Correct statement of the following C# code?

options.text: The subject class version of a() method gets called using sample class reference which holds subject class object
subject class hides a() method of base class
The code replaces the subject class version of a() with its math class version
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: The derived method is marked new, so it hides the virtual base method rather than overriding it. A maths reference still calls maths.a().

questions.question: Select the sequence of execution of function f1(), f2() & f3() in C# .NET CODE?

options.text:
f1() of derived class get executed
   f2() of derived class get executed
   f3() of base class get executed

f1() of base class get executed
   f2() of derived class get executed
   f3() of base class get executed

f1() of base class get executed
   f2() of derived class get executed
   f3() of derived class get executed

f1() of derived class get executed
   f2() of base class get executed
   f3() of base class get executed

questions.explanation: Through a baseclass reference: f1 is hidden so the base method runs; f2 is overridden so the derived method runs; f3 is hidden with new so the base virtual method runs.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Each derived class does not have its own version of a virtual method
If a derived class does not have its own version of virtual method then one in base class is used
By default methods are virtual
All of the mentioned

questions.explanation: C# instance methods are not virtual by default. If a derived class does not override a virtual method, the base implementation is used.

questions.question: Correct code to be added for overloaded operator - for the following C# code?

options.text: None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Unary operator - must be public static. Negating all components produces -5 -6 -8.

questions.question: Selecting appropriate method out of number of overloaded methods by matching arguments in terms of number, type and order and binding that selected method to object at compile time is called?

options.text: Static binding
Static Linking
Compile time polymorphism
All of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Choosing an overload from the argument list at compile time is compile-time polymorphism, also called static binding (early binding).

questions.question: Wrong statement about run time polymorphism is?

options.text: The overridden base method should be virtual, abstract or override
An abstract method is implicitly a virtual method
An abstract inherited property cannot be overridden in a derived class
Both override method and virtual method must have same access level modifier

questions.explanation: An abstract property (or method) can and typically must be overridden in a non-abstract derived class. a, b, and d are true of override/virtual/abstract.
